newsitem.title: ANGOLA: DE BEERS ANGOLAN GEM UNIT SHOULD HELP SECTOR.
newsitem.headline: DE BEERS ANGOLAN GEM UNIT SHOULD HELP SECTOR.

text.p: A planned De Beers Consolidated Mines diamond sorting facility in the Angolan capital should help to restore order to the country's diamond market, a senior De Beers official said Thursday.

"One of the problems we have been faced with in Angola is that there are no facilities," De Beers' Oliver Oliveira, Director of the Central Selling Office in London, told Reuters during a visit to Luanda.
"We hope that with this new plant we can help bring some order to the diamond industry in Angola," he added.

De Beers said on Tuesday it had signed an agreement with Angola's state diamond company Endiama to build a 12-storey building to house a purpose-built and secure diamond sorting facility for Angolan diamonds.
The $30 million building will be built on land leased from the national diamond company Endiama, which will own three floors of the new building in central Luanda.
Oliveira also said the current system of valuing diamonds in Angola was difficult to control and the company hoped to find a way to introduce a more scientific system.

"We need to bring a consistent system of valuation to this system," Oliveira said. "The current system is extremely hard to control. Endiama now values the diamonds, and they do not value the same way we do. We have something like 14,000 price points."
Oliveira said the new building would take up to three years to complete but would be a state-of-the-art structure.
"It will take us six months to get the building licences and about two-and-a-half years to build,' said Oliveira.

"But a building of this kind needs a lot of design," said Oliveira. "The lighting has to be just right and the security, of course, is important. We will have to have some very sophisticated security controls."
Angola produces around $1 billion in diamonds each year.
De Beers, which has four established buying offices in Angola, also has agreements with Endiama to prospect for new kimberlites in three areas.
